topics.label: Lecture framing: cancer hallmarks and learning aims
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's focus, learning outcomes, and approach to understanding cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Extracellular signaling pathways that regulate growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how external growth signals are transmitted and how mutations in Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinase, Ras–MAPK, PI3K–AKT, and TGF-beta pathways alter cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics show how impaired differentiation changes cancer cells, using hematological cancers and intestinal epithelium as examples.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how changes involving p53, Bax, and BCL2 can prevent cancer cells from undergoing apoptosis.

topics.label: Telomeres, senescence, and tumor-cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics connect telomere shortening to senescence and explain how TERT activation can help cancer cells bypass that replicative limit.

topics.label: p53 stress responses and growth-control hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The p53 discussion explains how cells respond to stress to protect genome integrity, and the following subtopic closes the account of mutation-driven growth-control hallmarks before moving on.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer-associated changes in glucose use and metabolism, including how altered metabolites can feed back on gene regulation through the epigenome.

topics.label: Angiogenesis in tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit vascular support and why angiogenesis can occur during tumor progression.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and establishment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace metastasis as the process by which tumor cells leave a primary site, survive the journey, and establish at distant sites, including how that process is detected and characterized.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion: shared cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing how diverse routes to cancer can produce shared hallmarks and by directing students to the next activities.
